document.title: Reagan Letter to Gandhi
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Reagan writes ahead of Gandhi's meeting with Zia ul-Haq about nuclear competition in the subcontinent. On Afghanistan, he says the U.S. told UN Secretary General Perez de Cuellar it was ready to accept the draft instrument on international guarantees, provided Soviet troop withdrawal is resolved.

key_claims: Reagan urged Gandhi to address nuclear competition with Pakistan in his talks with Zia on 17 Dec 1985.
The US stated readiness to act as guarantor of a comprehensive Afghanistan settlement, provided Soviet troop withdrawal is resolved.
The US informed UN Secretary General Pérez de Cuéllar in writing of readiness to accept the draft on international guarantees.
Reagan praised Gandhi's regional peace efforts including SAARC, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and new proposals to Pakistan.
Reagan sought continued improvement in Indo-US relations; the White House did not plan to release the text.
